narrative:
The model determined that you have an 88.3% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because the law school sets a high bar for predicted success, this probability led directly to the rejection of your application.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors, ranked by importance. Your first-year and third-year class rankings had the strongest influence, both pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. Being in the bottom decile for grades in both Year 1 and Year 3, compared to an average around the middle of the class among accepted students, signaled to the model that you would likely struggle with the demands of law school and the bar exam. Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor, but it worked mildly in the opposite direction, slightly lowering the predicted risk of failure because it was not extremely low.

Taken together, the model saw your consistently low class standing as the dominant signal that you were unlikely to pass the bar on the first try.

What you should do next is focus on improving your academic performance and building a stronger record. Consider retaking challenging courses, seeking tutoring, or gaining additional legal experience that demonstrates your ability to succeed. Strengthening these areas could significantly improve your profile for future applications. (218 words)
